design: Two matched paired runs, each version evaluated by two fresh-context agents. Each agent performs the same six tasks; task order is matched within each pair. A separate judge compares anonymized outputs without skill snapshots or version mapping.
case_author: Independent fresh-context agent; no access to baseline or candidate skill text.
candidate_policy: Freeze candidate and cases before both pairs. Preserve any later amendment as a separate revision and evaluation; do not silently pool it with these runs.
primary_question: Does the candidate reduce unjustified retained or added test obligations without losing contract protection, meaningful fault detection or useful healthy controls?
priority: Preserve supported contractual distinctions and authorized task scope.
Preserve detection of relevant non-equivalent seeded faults and survival of equivalent refactors.
Reduce redundant examples or obligations when they add no justified protection, boundary evidence or diagnosis.
Keep mutation work proportional and report its evidence honestly.
limitations: Small development sample, not a statistical superiority claim.
Multiple tasks within one agent session are not independent observations.
Behavioral folder isolation, not an operating-system confidentiality boundary.
Portable Python fixtures and supplied tool reports do not establish compatibility with every language or mutation framework.
No consuming application is changed or deployed.
decision_rule: Prefer retaining changes that show a concrete reduction in unjustified test obligations while preserving required distinctions, seeded-fault detection, equivalent-refactor survival and healthy controls. A tie is not a measured improvement. Any revision after results must be reported and evaluated separately rather than silently selecting favorable runs.
